page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine optimized for balanced compute and memory workloads. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, accompanied by 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware details include 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 execution units, VAES, and SHA_NI. The processor features a cache layout comprising 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 480 MB L3 cache.

In performance testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-threaded gzip compression performance at 36.47 GB/sec and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.05 GB/sec. Single-core stress-ng CPU tests, PassMark CPU testing (8649.88), and PassMark memory performance (2229.11) fall into average range tiers. Redis SET operations achieve 8.24 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 8.72 GB/sec. Multi-threaded CPU performance exhibits lower relative efficiency, with multi-core stress-ng results measuring 4653.8 and uncached large-block memory write bandwidth measuring 23.77 GB/sec.

The allocation of dedicated 4.2 GHz cores, 16 GB memory, and high-speed local NVMe storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-balanced operational workloads that require immediate local scratch space. Strong single-thread data manipulation capabilities and average memory throughput align this instance with application hosting, API backends, web serving, microservices, and streaming compression tasks.
